tips: Chapters XV-XVI (conjecture and hearsay) form one family: でしょう/だろう, かもしれない, みたいだ, ようだ, はずだ, らしい, そうだ all express degrees of certainty — drill them side by side rather than in isolation.
んです (XVII) is a register, not a new meaning: it recasts a plain statement as background explanation or invites one. Practice converting a plain-form sentence into its んです form.
そう/にする/になる (XVIII) split into two axes: そう is appearance-based conjecture (visual judgment), while にする/になる is state change (chosen vs. natural) — don't conflate them.
Relative clauses (XX) are the single biggest structural jump in N4: any plain-form clause can modify a noun directly, with no relative pronoun. Build long noun phrases from short ones first.

The giving/receiving + passive block (XXIII) is the densest chapter (11 points) — learn the verb pairs (貸す/借りる, 教える/教わる) before the passive forms; the passive builds directly on the same directionality logic.
